title: She Has Won Six of Eight World Cup Games Against Pakistan. Tomorrow, Harmanpreet Kaur Wants One More.
excerpt: India open their Women's T20 World Cup campaign against arch-rivals Pakistan at Edgbaston on Sunday — and Harmanpreet is calling for fearless cricket from ball one.
body:
The last time India lost to Pakistan at a Women's T20 World Cup, the margin was two runs. That was 2016 in Delhi, a decade ago. Since then, the Women in Blue have won three consecutive World Cup matches against their neighbours, each time more comfortably than the last.

On Sunday, June 14, at Edgbaston in Birmingham, the pattern will be tested again. India open their 2026 Women's T20 World Cup campaign against Pakistan in a Group 1 encounter that, on paper, should favour Harmanpreet Kaur's side. In practice, India-Pakistan cricket is never that simple.

Harmanpreet's Message: No Fear

Captain Harmanpreet Kaur set the tone after India's final warm-up match — a narrow five-run loss to hosts England in Cardiff on June 10. India fell short chasing 172, but Kaur saw more to like than to worry about.

"We are really looking forward to that," she said of the Pakistan fixture. "These two practice games have given us a lot of confidence, and even today, even though we lost the game, Richa batted well, and I think that's a big positive for us."

The "Richa" in question is Richa Ghosh, the explosive wicketkeeper-batter whose half-century almost pulled off an improbable chase against England's bowling attack. Ghosh's late-innings power has become one of India's most reliable weapons in the format.

"That's a big belief that if we stay on the pitch, we can turn the game anytime," Harmanpreet continued. "Hopefully we'll play our fearless cricket in our first game."

The Numbers Favour India — Heavily

The head-to-head record in T20 World Cups is stark: India lead 6-2 across eight meetings. Pakistan's last victory in the tournament came in 2016 in Delhi, where they scraped through by two runs. Before that, they won by a single run in 2012.

In the 2024 Women's T20 World Cup, India comfortably chased down Pakistan's target of 106, winning by six wickets with seven balls to spare. The gulf has widened as India's domestic cricket infrastructure — particularly the Women's Premier League — has accelerated the development of the squad.

Left-Arm Spin and the Edgbaston Pitch

India's coaching staff, led by Amol Muzumdar, has zeroed in on the left-arm spin threat for this campaign. "The T20 World Cup preparation started immediately after the last one," Muzumdar said. Edgbaston's surface historically offers assistance to slower bowlers, and India's spin arsenal — Deepti Sharma, Radha Yadav, and the all-round Shafali Verma — could prove decisive.

Former India cricketer Abhishek Nayar has suggested a likely playing XI: Shafali Verma, Smriti Mandhana, Yastika Bhatia, Jemimah Rodrigues, Harmanpreet Kaur, Richa Ghosh, Radha Yadav, Deepti Sharma, Arundhati Reddy, Sree Charani, and Kranti Gaud. If this combination clicks, India could set the tone for the entire tournament.

England Set the Standard

The tournament opened in dramatic fashion on June 12, when hosts England demolished Sri Lanka by 87 runs at Edgbaston. Danni Wyatt-Hodge scored an unbeaten 105 off 62 balls — the first century of the tournament and just the seventh in Women's T20 World Cup history. England posted 219/1, the highest innings total in the tournament's history, before bowling Sri Lanka out for 132.

It was a statement that England, unbeaten in World Cups at home, intend to make the most of the occasion. India will be watching closely.

The Bigger Picture: 2027 and Beyond

For India, this World Cup is not just about Pakistan or even the title. It is part of a longer arc towards the 2027 Women's ODI World Cup and India's ambitions as a global force in women's cricket. The WPL has transformed the depth of the Indian squad, and players like Ghosh, Shafali, and Jemimah Rodrigues have matured under sustained pressure in front of massive crowds.

How NRIs Can Watch

The match starts at 6:30 PM BST (1:30 PM ET / 10:30 AM PT) on Sunday, June 14 at Edgbaston Cricket Ground, Birmingham. For NRIs in the UK, tickets are still available through the ICC's official channels. For those in the US, the match will be available on Willow TV and streaming on Willow by Cricbuzz. In India, it airs on Star Sports.
